items.reason: The tool list holds no database function for this area. The area calls five open server addresses with no sign-in: feedback, help (AI answer), help rating, help replies and crash reports, plus voice-to-text. Each is limited per install and per network address per day, and the help AI has a monthly money ceiling. A rating or a reply is given only to the install that asked, holding a fresh random secret per question (tested). The one database function reached from here (the gym owner's Plus lock) runs with the member's own key. MettleUp Plus purchases are decided only on the phone with no server check: already filed.

The only server table this area reaches is the gym Plus-lock setting, through the member_plus_lock function. Apps cannot read the table at all: row rules on, no policy, every grant revoked; only key-checked functions touch it. The test that proves another gym is refused: after one owner switches the lock off, a member of a second gym still reads the default. The help and feedback messages sit in the panel's own small database, not in Supabase; there the test proves another install, or a wrong secret, gets nothing.
Rule applied: the one table this area reaches has a cross-gym test, so no table lacks one.
Rule applied: no live cross-gym attempt was run.

The secrets scan has no hit in these five folders and the key-pattern list for the area is empty. The web addresses here are public endpoints, the public GitHub releases page and licence pages; no key, token or password is written in the code.

No MettleUp AI key is in the app. The hidden AI coach takes the member's own OpenAI, Anthropic or Groq key and keeps it only in the phone's secure store. The help answers and voice-to-text use MettleUp's keys on the server only, with a monthly ceiling for help and daily caps for voice.
No sign-in, PIN or session is handled in these folders. The install id here is a random number for the help box, not a sign-in; the gym member key is only passed through from the shop folders.

Member text leaves only as JSON fields, cut to 2000 characters; the server treats it as data in the AI prompt. Phone database reads here use placeholders. A tapped notification can only open a plain in-app path, and an update link must start with the GitHub address.

The one upload is the spoken-feedback clip: sent to the voice box, which refuses a clip over 1 MB or an unknown sound type and caps clips per install, per network address and in total each day. The clip is deleted from the phone after sending. Picked pictures are only kept on the phone here.
No join code or gym page link is made or read here. Help replies are found only with a random per-question secret (two random ids joined), not a guessable number. App links open only fixed app pages.

Four files here use the screen-navigation library that the dependency scan flags high: already filed. The other libraries used here (secure store, file system, audio, crypto, state store) have no alert in the scan.
